title: Public candidate quality-metadata audit
scope: Current public one-shot candidate pools materialized from seed, DNA, reverse-pair, seam, and bridge data; unique by reading.

critical_limitation.finding: japanese_quality cannot currently be treated as an independent naturalness measurement.
reasons: Public DNA candidates receive quality mainly from layer in index.html (L1->A, L2->A-, L3->C).
The resulting L1 distribution is therefore tautological: all 492 default L1 candidates are labeled A.
Seed/seam/bridge records have more curated quality metadata, but pooling them with layer-derived DNA labels obscures the distinction.
critical_limitation.consequence: Do not report A/A- share as natural-language success rate.

valid_uses_of_current_metadata: Regression detection when a curated record changes layer/quality unexpectedly.
Comparing wrapper choices that already carry individually authored quality labels.
Filtering public layers according to existing product policy.
invalid_uses: Estimating the probability that a random generated sentence feels natural to a reader.
Claiming that all L1 DNA outputs are independently verified A-quality.
Comparing human naturalness between source types without new review.

next_step.proposal: Create a deterministic, source-stratified sample of public candidates and review each for grammaticality, semantic coherence, weirdness usefulness, and display/reading fidelity.
next_step.rule: Keep human review separate from the existing japanese_quality field until enough evidence exists to revise public labels.
